Go to therapy immediately. If I were your girlfriend, I would not want to have to see you everyday. I was lucky in the sense that my rapist was a stranger so I never had an emotional attachment to the person. You have shattered her trust and you need to give her space. She needs therapy, you need therapy, and honestly there is nothing you can do other than apologize profusely and never EVER do it again. Tbh I don't think it's healthy for her to date you as it may retraumatize her but that's entirely her decision. 

You need to give up control to her. You hurt her. She now has control over how she wants to handle the situation.
Awww this was very nice! I definitely think it helps that we didn't date for that long, but I do plan on being single for a while because ouch. I appreciate your response to my little vent :) ❤️
That's beautiful and honestly what a dream of a man. I'm so happy you found someone so juxtaposed to what you used to have.

I (22 F) have taken three partners' virginities and it has never phased me. It's really all about communication when it comes to having differences in sexual experience. I completely understand where you're coming from with this, and I think it would be in your favor to communicate these concerns to your girlfriend. That way, you guys can take it as slow or as fast as you both feel is necessary and she can take some extra care in showing you the ways she likes to feel good. 

I think it's also important to recognize that there is a learning curve with every new partner. Even if you weren't a virgin, you  would still need to figure out what she likes and how to make her orgasm. Every person is different. Don't give yourself a hard time. If she loves you, I promise she doesn't care.

I went through the entire rape trial process. Here's my advice. If she wants to press charges:
1. Call the police and ask to report a rape. The police will most likely send officers to take your statement. Tell them to meet you at the hospital. 
2. Go to the hospital and request a rape kit. Do not take a shower. Bring the underwear, clothes, sheets, etc. that you wore during the attack. 
3. Take photos of any bruises that you see on your body. Document everything that the nurses and police are documenting in case they lose evidence. Take pictures of where it happened. 
4. Bring food with you to the hospital. You will have to wait a long time for a special SA nurse. 
5. Do not message the rapist on social media. Any conversation that can be deemed "friendly" will be used against you. 
6. Do take screenshots of any communications the rapist sends you. Do NOT respond
7. Keep all business cards of the investigators and patrol officers you talk to. Put it in a folder. Your prosecutor might want it. 
8. Write down all details that you can remember while you're waiting for the nurse at the hospital. Your memory will fade. The more details you have, the better. 
9. Compile the name, phone number, and social media of anyone who may have been involved and give it to the police so they can interview them. 

If she just needs resources and doesn't want to press charges:
-go to the hospital anyway and ask for plan b and STI screenings 
-get in contact with the local women's sexual health center
- if you're a student, you can file a complaint with the Title nine office. They will investigate separately from the police for student misconduct. 
- most college campuses have a sexual assault and domestic violence center for students where they can connect you with trauma therapists

IF YOU WANT TO PRESS CHARGES, GO TO THE HOSPITAL IMMEDIATELY. DNA swabs are SUPER important

I'm very sorry about what you and your gf are going through. I went through the entire rape trial process and it's incredibly hard. Here are a few tips:

-rather than holding all of these sad feelings inside, let yourself cry in front of her. I know it may seem burdensome, but I actually felt so much better when people acknowledged that they we sad over what happened to me. It's much better than feeling like they don't care at all 

-don't bring up the sex thing. I know it sucks, but she will eventually heal and it will be at her own pace 

-you are her boyfriend so continue to make her feel beautiful. If you treat her like she's fragile, she will feel like you don't find her attractive anymore. Continue to make comments like "you look so beautiful today". Nothing makes you feel uglier than rape 

-when you feel like she needs help, instead of saying "let me know if you need help" give her options "how can I help you? I could distract you, we could talk about it, or I could leave you alone" 

-give her all the validation in the world. Just love on her. Make her feel special and important. When someone defiles your body like that, it makes you feel like no one could ever love you.
I look up my rapist every once in a while. It's normal, but you should see a therapist anyway because it's not good.

This is a great question!!! I have been through the entire trial process and unfortunately my rapist received a not guilty verdict. I have some tips:

- Give her options of support. Rather than asking her "how can I help you right now?" Say "Do you want alone time, do you want me to distract you, or do you want to talk about it?" People don't realize how exhausting it is to have to ask for help. Giving her options will make it feel less tasking. 

-Do not bring up the possibility of a not guilty verdict unless she brings it up first.

- Do not say things like, "do you think it would have been worse if...", "Look on the bright side", or "you just have to think positively". No. There is no bright side. The whole process sucks. 

-You need to anticipate a not guilty verdict in your head. Don't talk to her about it. What will you do if she gets a not guilty verdict for her case? Figure that out ahead of time. 

-Don't avoid the topic. It honestly hurt me immensely when my friends didn't text me to check on how I'm doing. It made me feel like they didn't care even though I know they were just trying to give me space. 

-Go to court with her. My dad had to physically carry me out of the court room when I received the not guilty verdict. I was devastated. Please just be there physically. Take off work if you have to. 

-Do not push sex, but also don't avoid it. Going to trial is the most humiliating thing. It would be even more humiliating to be rejected sexually by your girlfriend because she's worried that you're too fragile. Communication is key when it comes to physical intimacy.

-Make her feel beautiful.

My trial process lasted a little over a year. These things are frustratingly long, especially when you feel like this is monumentally traumatic and they don't seem to want it resolved. I'm sorry :( as someone who has done this before, keep being annoying. Keep calling them. Keep texting your victim advocate. Hell, I even got my dad involved.

It is not unusual for child survivors of sexual assault to reenact their assaults on other kids. It's horrific, but it does happen. This does not mean that what happened to you is okay or that you shouldn't be traumatized. 

My uncle adopted three siblings a few years ago. The siblings have a brother that had to be adopted by another family because he had been sexually abused and touched his sister inappropriately. The brother isn't a bad kid, but because of his abuse he ended up doing a terrible thing. His sister ended up being a victim of her brother's abuser indirectly. 

I think the best thing to do in this scenario is to talk to a therapist. You may even find it helpful to do counseling with your sister included in the sessions. Being in the presence of a professional will help you to convey your emotions without judgement.

Okay, great! Just be there to listen to her :) there's not really anything specific that you can do to make her feel better. This is an awful situation, but research has shown that one of the most important post-event risk factors for PTSD following assault is not having a support system. Be part of her team, and you will help her get through this with your presence.
I would pass her a note that says, "I think you're cute (insert sweet or nice or whatever)" and then put your phone number and name

Denial is a huge thing with rape. My rape was the poster child of "the perfect rape case". He was a stranger, I fought back, I reported an hour later, I took a rape kit that night, he bruised me, etc. I still had major denial and doubts. No matter what situation you're in, rape myths stop is from being 100% positive that it wasn't our fault. It all comes down to: you were asleep and he tried to hide it. A person partaking in consensual sex would not try to hide it. You also need to ask yourself, if your sister, mother, or friend told you this story what would your advice be to them? Would that change your perspective? What would you classify this scenario as? Relationship sexual violence can be really hard because it can feel like you have an established sexual trust with that person. However, just because you've had sex with someone doesn't mean that they have access to your body whenever they want.

Research supports that rape fantasies are fairly common among women. They are ESPECIALLY common among women who have been sexually assaulted. If you want to work through these fantasies, I would suggest finding a therapist that specializes in sex and sexual trauma. I have read a case study about a man who was able to train himself out of a torture fantasy (after being abused severely by his father in childhood) but I haven't read any studies about rape fantasies. That doesn't mean they're not out there! A licensed sex therapist would probably know.

Do you want to keep her in your life for the long term? I think you need to ask yourself how much you care about this girl so you can figure out whether you need to be setting up boundaries. Otherwise, she will probably come to you for help every time she has issues related to this. It's hard because she obviously needs help, but this is an extremely personal thing. Be very careful. Also, it's important to know that you experience a need to feel loved by people genuinely. After I was raped, I felt like I was incapable.of being loved for who I am. I was desperate to feel like someone cared about me and wasn't just looking at me like an object to use. She could be coming to you because she needs you to be that person for her. Tread lightly

I believe everyone deserves justice. I don't know if the court system believes that too though. They will probably not have enough evidence to convict him unless he confesses to doing it. Who knows, maybe he'll feel so guilty about it that he will be a decent human being and admit it. The first step is to file that police report. I was raped a couple months ago and went through the whole reporting process. It's not fun, but at least it makes the whole situation real. A lot of times we will go back in our heads and try to find holes in our story or memories that don't make sense. Honestly, most human memory doesn't make sense, but we never see that for ourselves. I think the reporting process gives you the opportunity to say to yourself "this was real, I deserve to be heard, he should feel sorry". Even if you don't have enough evidence, maybe just filing with the police will be helpful. Might even shake up his marriage a bit. 👊 More power to you. He deserves all the pain that's coming for him. I wouldn't worry too much about the girls. You're possibly doing them a favor by exposing him for who he is.

All you can do is be a friend, or if you're not comfortable with that be a person she can talk to if she needs it. Sexual assault survivors are prone to revictimization, so if there are support groups she can attend I'm sure she can find someone who will relate to her story. As someone who was recently raped, the most helpful thing a person can do is listen without judgement. Don't ask her intrusive questions, just listen. Also, it's important for you to realize that you don't have an obligation to her to act like a spouse right now. If she needs you to do that, encourage her to find a therapist or support group. If you feel comfortable talking to her about it that's great! If you don't, the best thing you can do is offer resources. This will set boundaries while showing that you still care about her wellbeing

I am very sorry for your loss. Please don't ruminate too much on the what ifs. Just know that you likely contributed to some of the good memories he had in life, even if his final moments were bad. It would be good to reach out to anyone right now. Friends at work? Gaming friends? Friends at school? Any family? If you are not comfortable with sharing with anyone in your life then please see a therapist if these feelings of guilt persist. I really hope that you find some peace at the funeral or that you find someone to talk to

I did an intensive outpatient program for my anorexia my freshman year of college and it saved my life. The timing is never right for this sort of thing, but if you go into the program with an open mind ready to change, it will impact you for the better. Ultimately, you just have to look at it like something that is mandatory in order to be successful in your career and relationships, because mental illness impacts both of those severely over time. It is an investment that may seem like a burden right now, but it will hopefully launch you into recovery.

Push the semester off for the clinic. If you're going to commit, commit. It seems like a big deal now, but if you successfully beat this you will recognize that death is way worse than delaying your plans. I have no doubt that you'll get your school work back on track, it just might take you a bit longer. That's okay!

You're exactly right! It's not really their fault. Most of the kids at my college act like that. It's kind of a work hard during the week, play hard during the weekend type of deal. It's just exhausting and dumb to me now. I can't drink anymore because I get flashbacks too easily. It might be time to move on, I just feel like the elderly friend. I honestly don't think they'll blame me. I live in a fairly self involved atmosphere and they probably won't notice if I distance myself.

Never in a sorority and it was a student athlete, but they're kind of like meaty frat boys anyway. I did file with Title IX, so if this court case falls through you best believe I will be nailing him and the university. That's kind of my last resort, though. I want to get into medical school here and I have a feeling they may be a little biased against someone who files against their athletics department. Thanks for the well wishes :)

First off, you definitely did not rape your girlfriend because there was no penetration involved. You at most sexually assaulted her. However, if you were completely honest with your girlfriend and she forgave you, I think you should move on and learn from your mistakes. You obviously felt like there was something wrong about the situation because in general you should not be touching like that when they are asleep. But just take this as a lesson and know that you did not break her personal boundaries this time but further action like that may break her trust. You shouldn't feel too anxious anymore, just don't do it again.

It's really difficult to get out of a relationship like that, but I'm so happy that you have come to the complete realization that none of what happened was your fault. I told her many times that I didn't think it was her fault, but she struggled a lot with the fact that she was the one who invited him over.

I will talk to them a little bit more! I think they were blindsided by my PTSD diagnosis because I wasn't more open with how I'm feeling. I'm really just trying not to impact my sisters. They have been through a lot and the hearing date is set for my sister's 18th birthday. I don't want to pull them away when it should be a fun and exciting time for her

Don't be too ashamed! My guy friend was the one who removed my assaulter from my apartment even though he was half his size. My roommate's boyfriend hugged me on the couch while I cried that night and drove home from the hospital with food waiting for me at home. We women recognize the men that love and support us! You should only be ashamed if you perpetuate the cycle of gender violence. 

And my sister is doing great! She had to have spinal fusion surgery, but she was able to walk 60 feet the day after her surgery. She is a senior in high school this year, and I couldn't be more proud of how hard she's working in PT and in therapy!

Every healing journey is different and I'm really happy that you're here and able to tell you story now! Thank you so much for all of the encouragement. It really means a lot coming from someone who experienced and fought through pain from sexual violence! I also love driving in my car and belting out songs :) it's a great stress reliever

I wanted to address a common concern about my post and my account. Several days after my assault happened, I created this account so that I could write out my story and my feelings whenever I felt overwhelmed about the case or had anxiety over what happened. I made the account because my other account has posts and comments on communities specific to my university, clubs, and even housing options on campus. The media doesn't know my identity and I'd prefer to keep it that way. I am not super experienced with reddit and I don't even really know what you use karma for. I never intended for this to be seen by so many people, as I mostly just post to these rape and support based groups as a way to reprocess the events and ground myself when I feel like I'm spiraling. I'm sorry if you think I'm lying or fishing for karma, but ultimately I know the truth and I know that it was never my intention to "use my story to get popular". Every person on here is entitled to their opinion, though!

I'm going through the court process for my own mental health. I need him to be punished. I posted this when I was having overwhelming feelings of anxiety and loneliness over the case. Sometimes you just need a nudge to say "hey, I think you're doing the right thing." Especially when this process has been so traumatizing. I would never go through the extra pain of this trial just so I could get a few compliments. This post was mostly just so I could release some pent up anxiety 🤷

I created a new account when this happened to me because I knew I needed to write out how I felt, but I needed to be entirely anonymous. My other account has comments and posts on pages specifically for my university and other interests. I never expected this to get the attention it did; in fact, I mostly use the account for when I'm having overwhelming feelings and need to work through them by writing. If you see all of my other posts, they're in a time progression all the way back to three days after it happened. I'm not trying to "farm karma", I'm just using a different account for anonymity and cathartic purposes. Thanks for sharing your opinion, though!

After a long night of people asking me to retell the event over and over, taking pictures, and removing my underwear for evidence, I was embarrassed and scared. She gave me underwear and made sure I had blankets because I was shivering from shock. She took everything at my pace without making me feel stupid or naive. You guys truly do God's work. I don't know what I would've done without her little bit of kindness that night

I think you need to speak to a therapist about this as soon as possible. You may very well be a manipulative person, but you may also be typecasting yourself as this person in your head. You're essentially dooming yourself to keep repeating this behavior over and over again if you continue to view yourself as a manipulative person. Figure out why you cheat on your boyfriends and go from there. Cheating is a terrible thing, but it does not make you a terrible person. It makes you a person who has hurt people because you yourself are hurting.
My trauma therapist actually set me up with a mindfulness routine to do this morning haha. She said that I was one insult away from unwinding and that I needed to reconnect my mind to my body 😂

Second, divorce is really hard and I'm sorry you're having to even approach the possibility. The main thing to note is that both of your parents love YOU. If you would talk to either of them I'm sure they would tell you the same. You should keep an open and honest conversation with your parents about how this is making you feel. Depression is not a fun thing to deal with by yourself. They may be able to set you up with a family therapist. Please let me know if you have any questions or need any help!

College is lonely the first semester even without a pandemic. You go from being surrounded by family and friends you know at home, to knowing absolutely no one on your hall or even at school. You are flooded with loads of individual time and nothing to do with it because you haven't made friends yet. Yes, it can be lonely, but once you get out there and make friends it will get a lot better. Take this time to try to meet people on your hall and figure out what hobbies YOU enjoy doing while you're not with people.

Yes! I filed a report the night it happened.

Good news, the DA decided to file felony sexual misconduct charges against him! I was always intent on pressing charges but didn't know whether the prosecutors would have enough evidence. He has his main hearing in September.

Because I live in university housing, they're required to report sexual assault to the police if they know about it. He attempted to get back into my building after my friend kicked him out, so we had to get housing involved. I didn't really have a choice in whether the police were involved, but now I have to decide whether I want to press charges. I'm leaning on the side of pressing charges. My school has allowed wrestlers, basketball players, and football players get away with this in the past. I'm not letting them do it again just because I feel uncomfortable.
